proof.text: Apply the derived coefficient adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] to the constant ring-sheaf map $A_Z\to B_Z$. The coefficient unit on $D$ gives a map $i_*A_D\to\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}(i_*B_D)$ by the direct-image functor, and its adjoint is precisely the specified morphism $\alpha_{A,B}:(i_*A_D)\otimes^\mathbf L_{A_Z}B_Z\to i_*B_D$. The normalization in the adjunction identifies this as the adjunct of $x\mapsto x\otimes1$.

proof.text: Take a geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z$. The closed immersion $i$ is finite: over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $Z$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $R/I$ is a cyclic $R$-module. Its geometric fibre $D\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_RR/I)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ (one point $\bar d$ over $\bar z$) if $\bar z$ lies on $D$ and is empty otherwise, as $\Omega\otimes_RR/I$ is a quotient of the field $\Omega$. By the finite-stalk formula [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] and the geometric stalk of a constant sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], the stalk of $i_*A_D$ at $\bar z$ is $(A_D)_{\bar d}=A$ when $\bar z$ lies on $D$ and is $0$ otherwise; likewise $(i_*B_D)_{\bar z}$ is $B$ or $0$, the map $(i_*A_D)_{\bar z}\to(i_*B_D)_{\bar z}$ induced by the coefficient unit is the ring map $A\to B$ or $0$, and $(B_Z)_{\bar z}=B$. On a K-flat flat-term representative $P$ of $i_*A_D$ the complex $P\otimes_{A_Z}B_Z$ computes both the change of rings and the derived tensor product over $A$ with $B_Z$; stalks are inverse images [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], which are monoidal [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]: the stalk of the derived tensor is $(i_*A_D)_{\bar z}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$, namely $A\otimes_AB=B$ on $D$ ($A$ is free of rank one) and $0$ off $D$. By the normalized adjunct formula $x\otimes b\mapsto b\,g(x)$ of Step 1, the stalk of $\alpha_{A,B}$ is the multiplication $A\otimes_AB\to B$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, an isomorphism, in the first case and the zero map $0\to0$ in the second. Stalks are exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so each $\mathcal H^q(\alpha_{A,B})$ is an isomorphism on all geometric stalks, hence an isomorphism [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], and $\alpha_{A,B}$ is a quasi-isomorphism (an isomorphism in $D(Z_{\Et},B)$) without any flatness assumption on $A\to B$.

proof.text: For a commutative square of coefficient maps $A\to B\to B'$, the coefficient units on $D$ and their direct images commute with the maps induced by $B\to B'$. The adjunction bijections are natural in both variables, and their normalized representative formula sends a map to the termwise balanced map $x\otimes b\mapsto b\,g(x)$. Therefore taking adjuncts shows that $\alpha_{A,B}$ is natural in the coefficient homomorphism.

proof.text: When the coefficient map is $A\to A$, the coefficient unit is the identity on $i_*A_D$. The normalized unit in [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] is represented by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, which is the identity under the canonical identification $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A\cong K$. Thus the stalkwise isomorphism of Step 2 is the identity and $\alpha_{A,A}=1$.

proof.text: Let $A\to B\to C$ be composable. On a K-flat flat-term representative $P$ of $i_*A_D$, the canonical transitivity map of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] is represented by $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto x\otimes b c$, and that node says that the composite of the two scalar-extension units equals the unit for $A\to C$. By the normalized adjunct formula of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], both $\alpha_{B,C}\circ(\alpha_{A,B}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)$ (transported across this transitivity isomorphism) and $\alpha_{A,C}$ are adjuncts of the same coefficient-unit map $i_*A_D\to\operatorname{Res}_{A\to C}(i_*C_D)$. Uniqueness of adjuncts gives the displayed composition identity, and the same argument gives coherence for iterated coefficient maps.

title: Derived scalar extension of a closed supported constant sheaf
statement:
Let $i:D\hookrightarrow Z$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $A\to B\to C$ be homomorphisms of finite commutative rings. Work on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], ordinary module direct image $i_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use derived scalar extension $-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ and its adjunction with termwise restriction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. The map $i_*A_D\to\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}(i_*B_D)$ induced by the coefficient unit has an adjunct
$$\alpha_{A,B}:(i_*A_D)\otimes_{A_Z}^{\mathbf L}B_Z\longrightarrow i_*B_D.$$
This specified comparison is an isomorphism. It is natural in the coefficient homomorphism, is the identity for $A\to A$, and satisfies
$$\alpha_{B,C}\circ(\alpha_{A,B}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)=\alpha_{A,C}\circ a_{A,B,C,i_*A_D},$$
where $a_{A,B,C,K}:(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C$ is the canonical transitivity isomorphism of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] for the constant ring sheaves $A_Z\to B_Z\to C_Z$. Neither coefficient homomorphism is assumed flat.
